input: Install a smart thermostat in the hallway

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is a brand-new install or a replacement of an existing thermostat changes what prep work, wiring checks, and removal steps are needed.
Whether the user plans to do this themselves or hire an electrician/HVAC technician determines how technical the plan needs to be and what safety guidance to include.
The type of heating/cooling system (e.g., single-stage, multi-stage, heat pump, combi boiler) dictates compatibility requirements and wiring complexity.
The user may already own a specific thermostat model, which fixes compatibility, wiring, and app requirements — or they may need purchasing guidance.
The presence or absence of a C-wire (common wire) is often the single biggest installation blocker for smart thermostats and changes the solution path significantly.
The user may prioritise specific features — e.g., voice assistant integration, energy reporting, scheduling — which affects which device or setup approach to recommend.
Understanding what 'done well' means — e.g., working app control, integration with a smart home hub, accurate scheduling — defines what testing and verification steps to include at the end.

gold.taskTitle: Install a smart thermostat in the hallway
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to replace or install a smart thermostat in their hallway, which involves choosing the right device, understanding the existing setup, and completing the physical installation.

questions.title: Is this replacing an old thermostat or a fresh install?
questions.description: Determine whether an existing thermostat needs to be removed and its wiring reused, or whether this is a completely new installation from scratch.

questions.title: Will you do this yourself or hire a professional?
questions.description: Establish whether the plan should be a DIY step-by-step guide or a checklist for briefing and supervising a tradesperson.

questions.title: What type of heating or cooling system do you have?
questions.description: Identify the HVAC or boiler system in use — e.g., forced air, heat pump, combi boiler, underfloor heating — to ensure thermostat compatibility.

questions.title: Do you already own a specific thermostat model?
questions.description: Find out if the user has already purchased a device (e.g., Nest, Ecobee, Honeywell) or still needs product selection guidance.

questions.title: Does your current wiring include a C-wire?
questions.description: Determine whether a common wire is present at the thermostat location, as its absence is the most frequent installation blocker for smart thermostats.

questions.title: Which smart home features matter most to you?
questions.description: Understand the user's priorities — such as voice control, energy usage reports, remote access, or integration with platforms like Alexa, Google Home, or Apple HomeKit.

questions.title: What does a successful install look like to you?
questions.description: Clarify the end goal — for example, stable app connectivity, correct scheduling, integration with an existing smart home system, or simply reliable temperature control.
